title: How I made a game using ONLY AI (full story in 15-min video)
author: Bj0rn_
selftext:
Hey guys!

My friend, Grolaf made Codex Mortis using only AI. I thought y'all may be interested in the process of making-of so I'm sharing his video.

In short - Codex Mortis is a survivors-like deckbuilder with mutating spells and ten schools of dark magic.

If you have any questions, feel free to ask \~

comments.author: insats
comments.body: Interesting recap! I wish him all the best. Tell him that Godot is actually very well suited for LLMs nowadays

replies.author: Bj0rn_
replies.body: The main problem with Godot on my first few tries was the programming language - it just somehow didn't want to work well for me. But truth be told, a year made a big difference, and now things run better whether it's Godot, Unity, or even Unreal. Still, when it comes to comfort of work, my favourite has stayed my own engine. Writing it kind of broke me in to that way of doing gamedev. Completely different challenges than using an off-the-shelf engine, and a massive injection of knowledge

replies.author: insats
replies.body:
Last time I checked, Unity was really not good for it. And Unreal is also very UI heavy.

The downside with javascript is being locked into the browser (which has a lower performance ceiling). I made games with React Native before switching to Godot and I wish I'd done it WAY sooner.

I did a lot of testing before I picked Godot my current project (which started in April). Couldn't be happier (and I've been a javascript dev for 15 years).

comments.author: rookan
comments.body: How did you create monsters animations?

replies.author: Bj0rn_
replies.body: For the animations I used PixelLab. they've got an animation model there and it works nicely. The mob sprites were made in different models over time, hence the art style is a bit all over the place, but all the animations went through PixelLab; Claude had access to the API key and I just batch-ran the whole lot through the API.
